unique.reason: Unvalidated needs value goes straight into the prompt and the result is cached; a crafted link could put false text on an official page, and the script lets any link set a11y_profile.
The simple page is short but not Easy Read: no explanations, no help, no year, Read aloud missing, and the link back comes after the form. A real barrier for the intended readers.
The unstyled link next to a button, with nothing saying what it does or what it records, leaves users unsure what will happen. A small burden.
The full text has long sentences and jargon and no map of where the bays move. A minor comprehension burden.
Neither page gives a contact, another way to respond or a route to other formats. Anyone the web form fails is excluded.
The whole page is one utterance, a known Chrome cutoff applies, and nothing handles an error, so reading can stop silently before the blue badge facts.
The simple page has no heading before its form and no instructions, so the form is hard to find by heading and guidance is missing. Minor.
The radio group is not required and answers are lost when switching versions. Real but fairly minor; the closing-time point is marginal.
The dropped hours and all-traffic caveat make the simple text say the opposite of the proposal, which plainly misinforms respondents.
The simple text turns a proposal into settled fact ('will'), so readers may think it is decided. A material loss of meaning.
The hedged modelled estimate becomes a flat claim and the cost to car journeys is dropped. The trade-off is lost and the text leans one way.
A hidden, hard-coded learning-disability label is stored with each response and exported by profile without notice. This discloses an implied disability, and the data is also false.
Sending the whole page to the service with no list of what must be kept is a real process gap, but it is indirect and partly self-referential about the reviewers.
The week-long cache with no source stamp could serve text from a superseded original. Plausible but contingent.
IP logs, uid, a11y_profile and comments could be joined to re-identify disabled respondents, and small groups in a local consultation make that worse. A real privacy exposure.
Mostly commentary on the reviewers' own untested predictions and on measurement philosophy; little concrete basis in the material beyond points already made elsewhere.
